I have farmed this half-hectare since I was a boy and I own it, so I take care of it. Last season I put half a 100kg bag of DAP on this plot and the heads were fuller than my brother’s, so this year I will do the same — it is what I can afford after paying for ox-ploughing. I will also spread two cartloads of manure from my cattle before planting, because my father always said owned land deserves dung. I will plant my own saved red maize seed, not the new packets from the cooperative, because I saw my neighbor’s hybrid crop dry out two years ago when the rains stopped early; my wife and sons will do the weeding and harvesting ourselves, and we will spend about forty days on this plot between ploughing, weeding, and carrying the harvest home.
